about: The benches station: a 72 x 30 in, 1.75 in maple butcher-block workbench on a 2 in square-tube frame (levelling feet, angle rails, a notched lower shelf), a six-drawer modular cabinet (Lista-style full-width aluminium handles with label cards) standing on the shelf under its left end, and a 30 x 18 in two-tray steel utility cart on 3 in swivel casters with a push handle. Self-made in Blender (sources/bench/build_bench.py), every part where the library placeholder (planner.placeholders.workbench_set) has its box, in the step videos' colours (look.py: cart_red, frame_black). Props: two hopper bins on the shelf, a tool box, a tray of finished parts, a deburring tool and a file on the cart; nothing on the bench top, which the steps use.
reviewed: 2026-11-05: modelled; look sheets and three.js before/after checked

source.made: self-made in Blender from public dimensions and photos; build script and .blend beside it

sources_used: Global Industrial / Zoro listings, 72 x 30 in maple butcher-block workbenches: 1.75 in square-edge top, 34 in high, 2 in square or 1-5/8 in round legs, lower shelf, levelling feet
Zoro / Global Industrial steel utility carts, 30 x 18 in, two lipped trays (1.5 in lips), 3-5 in casters
Lista / Vidmar modular drawer cabinets (full-width extruded aluminium drawer pulls with label slots); Akro-Mils 30240 hopper bins (14.75 x 8.25 x 7 in)
the library record and placeholder (bench.glb) for every part's position

unsure.what: the frame colour: kept near-black to match the step videos (look.py frame_black); most catalogue benches are grey or blue
the cabinet's six drawer heights are a typical mix, scaled to the placeholder's box

atlas_why: 2048 rather than the hero class's 4096: at 16k triangles of mostly flat sheet and wood the AO is ~3 mm a texel either way visually the same, and it saves 1.3 MB of download and 17 MB of GPU memory
double_sided_why: self-made closed solids, normals checked outward when built (jig.orient), hidden faces culled: single-sided saves fill rate
